thread.title: Special Participation B: Gemini in Colab on Homework 5
thread.content: <document version="2.0"><paragraph>I used Gemini within Google Colab on the coding questions in HW 5. Gemini eventually converged to a correct, reference-matching solution and achieved the expected accuracy, but the path was bumpy: it got tripped up by environment and TypeErrors, occasionally lost context, and needed several retries to settle on the right batchnorm, pooling, dropout, and conv forward/backward logic. It followed the reference architecture once nudged, so while it was competent and capable of matching the spec, it required manual guidance to resolve confusion and code-environment hiccups, so its productivity was lower than it could have been.</paragraph><paragraph/><paragraph>Chat logs and notes:</paragraph><file url="https://static.us.edusercontent.com/files/l77HlRbXego1J3rCrsdFfwke" filename="pytorch_cnn.ipynb - Colab.pdf"/><file url="https://static.us.edusercontent.com/files/Cv9ADSVIquSefTA6ZY3kP8GB" filename="cnn.ipynb - Colab.pdf"/><file url="https://static.us.edusercontent.com/files/OXckSzcXukBwTkivK6SJzNml" filename="q_coding_dropout.ipynb - Colab.pdf"/><file url="https://static.us.edusercontent.com/files/Z0yWh5fXD0kkvNnxH6B6vxJB" filename="bn_drop.ipynb - Colab.pdf"/><paragraph/></document>
thread.document:
I used Gemini within Google Colab on the coding questions in HW 5. Gemini eventually converged to a correct, reference-matching solution and achieved the expected accuracy, but the path was bumpy: it got tripped up by environment and TypeErrors, occasionally lost context, and needed several retries to settle on the right batchnorm, pooling, dropout, and conv forward/backward logic. It followed the reference architecture once nudged, so while it was competent and capable of matching the spec, it required manual guidance to resolve confusion and code-environment hiccups, so its productivity was lower than it could have been.
